title: Two-dimensional solitons in extended GPE models with Lee-Huang-Yang corrections
authors: G. N. Koutsokostas, F. Bristy, E. C. Psychogiou, G. A. Bougas, G. C. Katsimiga, S. I. Mistakidis, P. G. Kevrekidis, D. J. Frantzeskakis
abstract: We investigate the existence and dynamics of two-dimensional solitary waves in a quantum droplet environment described by the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation featuring logarithmic mean-field and Lee-Huang-Yang interactions. In the modulationally stable regime of the background, we employ suitable multiscale asymptotic methods to derive effective nonlinear integrable models corresponding to the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili and Davey-Stewartson equations. Based on these reduced models, we construct approximate analytical solutions describing line solitons, algebraically localized lump solitons, ring solitons, and exponentially localized dromions embedded on the droplet background. The dynamical robustness of these solutions is monitored through numerical simulations. Line, lump and ring solitons stay closest to the theoretical predictions, although progressively deviate due to the emergence of small-amplitude radiation, while dromions depart from their analytical waveform the most, although they roughly maintain their shape. Our results unveil unprecedented multidimensional soliton solutions in models featuring the competition of mean-field and quantum fluctuations and as such are amenable to current ultracold atom experiments.
summary: The paper analyzes 2D solitons in quantum droplets governed by an extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation that includes Lee-Huang-Yang corrections. By using multiscale asymptotic methods, the complex dynamics are reduced to integrable models like KP and DS equations. The results provide approximate analytical solutions for various soliton shapes, confirming their potential observability in current ultracold atom experiments.
main_problem: Investigating the existence and dynamics of two-dimensional solitary waves (solitons) within a quantum droplet environment.
main_result: The study constructs approximate analytical solutions for various soliton types (line, lump, ring, dromion), revealing unprecedented multidimensional solutions in models balancing mean-field and quantum fluctuations.
method: Multiscale asymptotic methods are employed to reduce the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE) to effective integrable nonlinear models like KP and Davey-Stewartson equations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a 2D eGPE incorporating logarithmic mean-field and Lee-Huang-Yang interactions, describing quantum droplets in an ultracold atom setting. The analysis focuses on excitations above the modulationally stable background state.
key_observables: Line solitons, algebraically localized lump solitons, ring solitons, and exponentially localized dromions embedded on the droplet background.
important_parameters: The competition between mean-field interactions and quantum fluctuations; operation in the modulationally stable regime ($\delta a \lesssim 0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on asymptotic expansions (small amplitude excitations $\epsilon \ll 1$) and assumes the background state is modulationally stable.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates density contours for various soliton solutions, including ring, line, lump, and dromion examples.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by introducing the 2D eGPE (Sec. II), analyzing modulational stability, reducing it to integrable models using multiscale analysis (Sec. III), constructing approximate solutions (Sec. IV), and concluding with a summary (Sec. V).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses nonlinear wave phenomena in quantum matter systems relevant to ultracold atom experiments, bridging mean-field theory with quantum fluctuation corrections.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The upper and lower branches of the Lambert W function (see legend) with respect to scaled chemical potential µ/g. The upper (lower) branch is associated to modulational stable (unstable) droplet background. The 2D solitons (see also Fig. 2) exist on the modulationally stable branch. The horizontal and vertical pink solid lines mark the W(µ/g) = 0 and µ = 0 cases respectively.

FIG. 2. Density contours and theoretical projections along the x-y plane corresponding to the different solitary wave solutions. The parameters for the ring-soliton are g = 1, ξ0 = 1, ϵ = 0.1, κ1 = 1, ρ0 = 1 in Eq. (36a); for the line soliton the parameters are g = 1, ξ0 = 0, ϵ = 0.1, κ1 = 1, κ2 = 0, ρ0 = 1 in Eq. (32a). For the lump soliton, we use g = 1, ϵ = 0.1, λ1 = 0, λ2 = 1, ρ0 = 1 in Eq. (33), and for the dromion the parameter values are g = 1, ϵ = 0.01, k = 1.2, ρ0 = 2.25, A = −0.22, c0 = −6.48, c1 = −1.35, c2 = −6.15, c3 = −28.64, c4 = 14.30 in Eq. (37).

FIG. 3. Spatiotemporal density evolution of the 2D line soliton described by Eq. (32a) at selected time-instants (see legends). (a)-(e) 2D density profiles |Ψ(x, y)|2, and (f)-(j) the corresponding 1D density cross-sections along x at y = 0 (blue solid line and left axis) together with the associated wavefunction phase Arg[ψ(x, 0)] (dashed orange lines and right axis). The moving 2D line soliton propagates to the left, while emitting a relatively small amount of radiation. The characteristics of the initial line soliton at t = 0 are g = 1, ξ0 = 0, ϵ = 0.1, κ1 = 1.2, κ2 = 0, ρ0 = 1 respectively.
